objects.split_method: walk-forward by time plus held-out technology family where feasible
objects.point_in_time_policy: All releases, denominators and revisions use first-available timestamps and vintage-aware reconstruction.
objects.multiple_testing_policy: Pre-register transformations; adjust family-wise discovery or false-discovery rate when screening multiple definitions.
objects.calibration_requirement: If probabilities are emitted, reliability and Brier/log loss must be reported; otherwise state-transition frequencies must be calibrated.
objects.regime_holdout: At least one unseen technology family or macro funding regime.
objects.acceptance_threshold: Must beat simpler baseline out of sample on primary metric without material stability or missingness deterioration; no weighted aggregate score.
objects.complexity_penalty: Prefer the simplest specification within one standard-error-equivalent performance band.

objects.split_method: rolling/expanding walk-forward by narrative and time
objects.point_in_time_policy: Only text and model versions available by cutoff; source universe and labels version-pinned.
objects.multiple_testing_policy: Topic/narrative definitions frozen before each test fold; control FDR when scanning many narratives.
objects.calibration_requirement: Probability outputs require reliability curves and calibration error; turning-point outputs require false-alarm accounting.
objects.regime_holdout: Hold out at least one narrative family or market regime.
objects.acceptance_threshold: Incremental OOS improvement versus level-only baseline on calibration or turning-point metric with no unacceptable false-alarm increase.
objects.complexity_penalty: Penalize extra topic features, contagion parameters and model states unless OOS lift is stable.

objects.split_method: cross-sectional time-series walk-forward with industry holdouts
objects.point_in_time_policy: Company and industry fundamentals use publication-date vintages; future winner labels are never backfilled into features.
objects.multiple_testing_policy: Pre-register factor definitions and tail labels; control FDR across variants.
objects.calibration_requirement: If winner probabilities are produced, report calibration; otherwise report bucket frequencies with confidence intervals.
objects.regime_holdout: Hold out industries with different capital intensity/network structures.
objects.acceptance_threshold: Must improve top-tail precision or wealth-tail recall over simple size/share baselines without relying on a single industry.
objects.complexity_penalty: Prefer interpretable factor structures; penalize feature proliferation relative to sample tail count.

objects.split_method: nested walk-forward; threshold/model selection inside training folds only
objects.point_in_time_policy: All conditioning variables and event definitions are PIT; revised macro/fundamental data use vintages.
objects.multiple_testing_policy: Tail thresholds and feature sets are preregistered or corrected for search within training folds.
objects.calibration_requirement: Mandatory reliability/calibration analysis for rare-event probabilities; raw accuracy is prohibited as a primary metric.
objects.regime_holdout: Hold out at least one crisis/non-crisis regime and one asset family where sample permits.
objects.acceptance_threshold: Must improve calibration or precision-recall versus unconditional baselines while controlling false alarms; no claim of black-swan certainty.
objects.complexity_penalty: Penalize latent states/features relative to extreme-event count; simpler calibrated model wins ties.

objects.split_method: historical PIT replay plus scenario stress by instrument family
objects.point_in_time_policy: Use observed contemporaneous premiums, IV and transaction-cost proxies; no later quote substitution.
objects.multiple_testing_policy: Instrument/tenor selection rules frozen before replay; control selection bias across large option grids.
objects.calibration_requirement: Scenario probabilities must be labeled assumed vs estimated; estimated distributions require calibration diagnostics.
objects.regime_holdout: Include high-volatility, low-liquidity and gap regimes.
objects.acceptance_threshold: Net asymmetry must remain favorable relative to matched linear baseline across declared sensitivity band; contractual downside assumptions must survive implementation stress.
objects.complexity_penalty: Penalize multi-leg complexity, turnover and liquidity dependence.

objects.split_method: PIT cross-sectional walk-forward by sector and valuation regime
objects.point_in_time_policy: Enterprise value and financials use original publication dates; discount assumptions versioned at analysis time.
objects.multiple_testing_policy: Scenario grids and terminal assumptions preregistered; no ex-post parameter tuning to realized price.
objects.calibration_requirement: Where probability states are emitted, calibration required; otherwise report empirical outcome frequencies by implied-expectation state.
objects.regime_holdout: Hold out at least one high-rate/low-rate or high-growth/low-growth regime.
objects.acceptance_threshold: Must add stable expectation-gap information beyond simple multiples under reasonable sensitivity ranges; target-price accuracy is not a benchmark.
objects.complexity_penalty: Penalize terminal-value dominance and parameter degrees of freedom.

objects.split_method: walk-forward portfolio replay plus synthetic tail/liquidity stress
objects.point_in_time_policy: Positions, exposures, prices and liquidity assumptions use contemporaneous state only.
objects.multiple_testing_policy: Constraint sets and sizing variants preregistered; avoid selecting on realized terminal wealth alone.
objects.calibration_requirement: Stress frequencies and simulated ruin probabilities must be compared with realized/held-out breach frequencies where possible.
objects.regime_holdout: Include crisis, correlation-spike and liquidity-contraction regimes.
objects.acceptance_threshold: Must reduce ruin/breach outcomes versus aggressive baseline while preserving material geometric growth and passing explicit hard constraints.
objects.complexity_penalty: Prefer fewer robust constraints and transparent sizing rules over highly tuned scenario-specific policies.
